title: Groundnut — Harvest, Yield and Post-Harvest Management
content:
GROUNDNUT HARVEST:

MATURITY INDICATORS:
- Inner skin of pods turns dark (pink to red to dark red).
- 80% of pods show dark veins inside shell when broken.
- Plant foliage begins to yellow and wilt.
- Kernel fills the pod completely.
- Days to maturity: 95-110 days (kharif), 110-130 days (rabi).

HARVEST METHOD:
- Manual uprooting: Traditional method for small farmers.
- Mechanical: Tractor-mounted digger-shaker for larger areas.
- Harvest when soil is slightly moist — dry soil causes pod shattering.
- Best harvested in early morning.

THRESHING:
- Mechanical pod stripper after 1-2 days field windrow drying.
- Manual beating is traditional. Avoid over-beating (splits pods).

DRYING:
- Sun dry pods 7-10 days to reduce moisture to 8-9%.
- Heap drying in field: Place uprooted plants in windrows for 3-5 days.
- Target moisture for safe storage: 8-9% (pods), 7-8% (kernels).

STORAGE:
- Store in gunny bags in well-ventilated, dry godown.
- Stack on wooden pallets — avoid floor contact.
- Temperature: 5-10°C for long storage.
- Fumigate with Aluminium Phosphide @ 3 tablets (3g)/tonne in sealed storage.
- Do not store with high moisture — aflatoxin contamination risk.

YIELD POTENTIAL:
- Kharif (irrigated): 2.5–3.5 t/ha pods.
- Kharif (rainfed): 1.5–2.5 t/ha pods.
- Rabi (irrigated): 3.0–4.0 t/ha pods.
- Highest yielding variety GPBD-4 under good management: up to 4 t/ha.
